entry.title: Pokémon Stamp Mini-Sheet Goes on Sale November 20, with a Total Issue of 300,000 Sheets (translated)
entry.summary: The Pokémon stamp mini-sheet is scheduled to go on sale on November 20, with an issue of 300,000 sheets. Each sheet contains 10 stamps and is being released in conjunction with the 2026 Taipei World Stamp Championship. The product brings the Pokémon game IP into the postal collectibles market once again, giving collectors another physical option for commemorating it.

entry.title: Cooperative board game Tangled Yarns surpasses its crowdfunding goal by more than six times, Japanese rulebook released (translated)
entry.summary: Tangled Yarns has raised more than six times its original crowdfunding goal, growing from $5,000 to over $34,000. This reflects the continued and clear appeal of cosmic horror in the cooperative board-game market. The campaign is scheduled to run until October 1, so early backers are also becoming part of the game's subsequent development.

entry.title: Indoor Gardening Simulation Game Tiny Eden Launches on Steam After Surpassing 150,000 Wishlists (translated)
entry.summary: Tiny Eden accumulated more than 150,000 wishlists before launching on Steam, and officially released today. Set in a futuristic city apartment, the game lets players grow plants, cook and sell their produce, then gradually expand their indoor farm; it places slow-paced life management within limited living space, making the farm’s growth the core of ongoing play.

entry.title: Mythic Monster Launches on Steam, Bringing Mythical Monster Parties to a Demon Lord Hunt (translated)
entry.summary: Mythic Monster is now available on Steam for 980 yen, placing mythical monster parties, gear grinding, and strategic combat within the same compact adventure framework. The game was released by Kodansha Creators' Lab; its price lowers the barrier to trying a new concept, while its core appeal still depends on whether players enjoy this blend of collecting, progression, and tactical decision-making.

entry.title: Onimusha Sells Over One Million on Launch Day as Capcom Speeds Up Revival of Dormant IP (translated)
entry.summary: Onimusha: Way of the Sword sold more than 1 million copies worldwide on its launch day. The new entry in the series, which returned after an absence of more than 20 years, also helped push cumulative sales of the Onimusha series past 10 million copies. Capcom said the result shows that IPs without a new release for a long time may still have a market, so it will include its extensive library in its plans to reactivate dormant properties; other long-quiet series, such as Dino Crisis, have consequently drawn attention again.

entry.title: Classic RTS Tactical Commanders R to Return via Steam (translated)
entry.summary: The Steam store page for Tactical Commanders R is now live. Developed by Choga Software, this remake carries on the systems of Nexon's classic RTS Tactical Commanders and is expected to hold a small-scale closed beta test between September and October. The game retains its core focus on large-scale real-time strategy, troop command, positional deployment, team battles, and cooperation, while also planning to add new elements without undermining the original's appeal; an official release date has not yet been announced.

entry.title: Pokémon GO: Oricorio Makes Its Debut as Max Battles and Mega Evolution Events Unlock (translated)
entry.summary: The “Team GO Mega” event in Pokémon GO will run from September 8 at 10:00 to September 14 at 20:00. During the event, Falinks and its evolved form, Maushold, will make their first appearance, while a Shiny version of Squawkabilly will also be added to the collection targets. The event will also allow Mega Beedrill and Mega Houndoom to reach the Gigantamax level and will add corresponding special moves; players will need to obtain the related content through Eggs, Field Research, wild encounters, and raids.

entry.title: Japanese Media Reports USJ Universal Studios Japan Confirms New Pokémon-Themed Area (translated)
entry.summary: Universal Studios Japan has confirmed that it will work with Pokémon-related parties to create a themed area, giving the game world another entrance that people can actually walk into. What is known at this stage is the partnership and the planning of the themed area, which has also prompted players to imagine what the future experience might be like; the opening date and the facilities included will directly affect the scale and appeal of the partnership in its final form.

entry.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky the 2nd Hands-On: Watching Estelle and Her Companions Continue to Grow (translated)
entry.summary: Building on the successful remake of the previous game, The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky the 2nd continues the original story and system framework while adding new content. This hands-on preview focuses on character growth and the experience offered by the complete PC version in actual play, giving familiar players a chance to reconsider how the remake handles an established journey while showing new players how to enter this long-form adventure.

entry.title: Chuplay Strange Talk: How to Handle the Oppressive Feeling of Game Creation (translated)
entry.summary: When a game creator’s self-expression comes into tension with market expectations, there is still no simple answer to the question of whom a work should respond to first. Starting from common stereotypes in wuxia games, the article expands the discussion to how indie and single-player games can find their place among preserving creative individuality, helping players understand the design, and keeping the work viable.

entry.title: “The World’s Number One Hai Dou Tournament”: Teams Learn to Trust Their Own Playstyle (translated)
entry.summary: The League of Legends Hai Dou Tournament teams advanced from online qualifiers to a training camp in Shanghai, gradually adjusting the pace of their games amid qualification calculations, an unfamiliar format, and the pressure of elimination. The article records how the players faced a new competitive environment, while focusing on how they established ways to control matches through in-game judgement and teamwork.

entry.title: Heartstop Town Brings Its Back-to-School Charity Initiative to a Rural School (translated)
entry.summary: On September 4, Heartstop Town launched the charitable education-support initiative “A Token of Care from the Town,” bringing the spirit of mutual aid among neighbours from the game to Dayaosao Primary School in Nanping Town, Guangnan County, Wenshan Prefecture, Yunnan Province. The team donated desks and chairs, daily necessities for students, basketballs, badminton equipment and art supplies, and also arranged sports activities and art lessons to respond to rural children’s needs in learning, daily life and emotional companionship.

entry.title: Dreadline Express Brings Lovecraftian Horror Aboard the Last Human Train (translated)
entry.summary: Polygon writer Ford James tried the debut work of independent developer David Konecny, Dreadline Express, at Gamescom 2026. The game combines humanity’s struggle to survive aboard an apocalyptic train with Lovecraftian horror, PSX-era visuals, and passengers gradually descending into madness; players explore to collect clues and knowledge cards, gaining more possible actions as they interact and slowly unravel the mystery of the last train carrying humanity.

entry.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Improves DLSS 5 Performance with Two Graphics Cards (translated)
entry.summary: After applying DLSS 5, The Blood of Dawnwalker gains more detailed visuals, but at a very high performance cost. A mod author has gone a step further and found a way to distribute the graphics-card workload, allowing players to readjust the trade-off between finer image quality and hardware requirements.

entry.title: Dozens of Crytek employees reportedly laid off after Crysis 4 cancellation (translated)
entry.summary: After Crysis 4 was cancelled, dozens more employees were reportedly laid off from Crytek's offices in Istanbul and Frankfurt in early September, with workers described as having been caught off guard. The consequences of the cancellation have therefore extended to the development team, affecting more than just the game players had originally been looking forward to.

entry.title: Which Mods Are Worth Using in The Blood of Dawnwalker? (translated)
entry.summary: Jeuxvideo.com has compiled the PC mod options for The Blood of Dawnwalker, selecting tools from Nexus Mods that can significantly change the way the game is played and explaining how to install them. The guide covers adjustments such as extending or simplifying the 30-day time limit and increasing the carrying-capacity limit, allowing players to tailor their RPG experience to their own hardware and playing pace; mods have therefore become a common part of PC gaming culture.

entry.title: Miami-Dade County Wants to Market the City Through GTA 6, but Faces Opposition from the Sheriff and Council Members (translated)
entry.summary: GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on November 19, and Miami-Dade County had initially envisioned working with Rockstar to give airport baggage carousels, welcome signs, Metromover trains, and manhole covers a game-inspired makeover, thereby attracting players eager to visit and boosting tourism. However, Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz, council member Juan Carlos Bermudez, and judicial authorities oppose having the public sector promote a game depicting crime and violence, while the county government says the partnership has not yet been formally approved. Meanwhile, the City of Miami is preparing to vote on a temporary ordinance on September 10. If passed, it would relax advertising regulations from October 15 through December 31, allowing Rockstar to compete for six advertising sites in the city center and bringing an estimated $1.2 million-plus to the city treasury; it remains uncertain whether the ordinance will pass.

entry.title: 3 Games That Truly Give Weight to Player Choices (translated)
entry.summary: The article revisits what it means for choices to matter in games, arguing that although large branching structures and multiple endings create a strong sense of impact, the format has gradually become formulaic. It therefore introduces three works that respond to player decisions in different ways. In Zero Parades: For Dead Spies, character abilities affect dialogue checks and the way players understand events; even seemingly fatal decisions usually leave a way forward. In Slay the Princess, refusing to enter the cabin also counts as a valid choice and opens a new story branch. Last Defense Academy has 100 endings, and none of them is treated as canon.

entry.title: GTA Cheat Codes Taught a Generation of Players That Breaking the Rules Can Be Great Fun (translated)
entry.summary: The article looks back at GTA cheat codes in the PS2 era. The author shares how they used familiar weapon codes to skip the intended progression, and how they and friends turned the game into a sandbox experiment: pushing the wanted level to its maximum and watching how the city responded. This way of playing could certainly cause players to miss Rockstar’s satirical storytelling, and it once deepened the wider moral panic around violence in games. But the article argues that cheat codes let players explore an open world that responds to chaos according to their own rules, rather than merely destroying their progress. It treats playing outside the intended design as one way to understand the vitality of a system.

entry.title: FEEDSTOCK Reveals Its Steam Store Page: The More You Carry, the Bigger Your Partner Gets—and the Harder It Is to Retreat (translated)
entry.summary: Ahaha studio revealed FEEDSTOCK’s Steam store page on September 6, with a planned release in October 2026. It is a first-person cooperative horror game for up to four players. Players feed recovered items to their companion, Tally, in exchange for materials, which can then be sold to expand their equipment; but the more Tally eats, the larger it becomes, so a door it could pass through on the way in may be impossible to pass through on the way back. Making it spit out some of the items also costs corresponding resources. The game supports proximity voice chat and requires a microphone because Tally follows players who are speaking. There are four types of enemies inside, each responding to a different noise threshold. The game provides no weapons, and enemies cannot be knocked down.

entry.title: Chain Chronicle Adds Lancelot, Who Has Obtained the Power of the Otherworldly God (translated)
entry.summary: Chain Chronicle will hold the “Otherworldly God Liberation Festival” from September 6 at 11:00 to September 15 at 10:59. The featured character is Lancelot, who has obtained the power of the otherworldly god, voiced by Ryotaro Okiayu, and he can be acquired through a limited-time gacha. The official announcement also detailed the pull-reward ladder: 10 pulls grant a premium ticket; starting at 20 and 30 pulls, free ten-pulls and a guaranteed SSR are unlocked in succession; 100 pulls directly grant the character; and 120 and 150 pulls provide additional SSR exchange rewards. During the event, the game will also offer a trial quest for the new character, training quests, daily weapon-material quests, and reruns of the “Chronicle’s Awakening” characters and event quests featuring Lancelot.

entry.title: Hearts of Iron IV’s Major Expansion Is Delayed as Paradox Adopts a New Release Approach (translated)
entry.summary: Paradox announced that it is delaying the next major expansion for Hearts of Iron IV because it needs more time to polish it. The previous paid expansion, Thunder at our Gates, received 70% negative reviews on Steam. Players had also criticised several earlier DLCs for being too buggy and for charging for shallow content that should have arrived as part of a free update. The studio said development diaries introducing the new DLC will begin earlier than in previous years so that player feedback can be collected sooner, while the concluding update for Thunder at our Gates will arrive on schedule. The current plan is as follows: update 1.19.3 launches on September 17 with Australian Underground and Indonesia and Siam content; Romania content will later receive a patch aimed at reducing clicks and information overload; and the next Expansion Pass, hinted to focus on the United States, will be postponed until after that content.

entry.title: Guild Wars 3 PC Preview: It Might Revive MMORPGs (translated)
entry.summary: Guild Wars 3 appeared at Gamescom 2026 in a roughly 20-minute hands-off preview, showcasing movement and combat systems that are still in the pre-alpha stage. The preview placed particular emphasis on three-dimensional terrain, stamina-free climbing and gliding, and momentum that affects attack damage; in co-op, a warrior’s shield can serve as a springboard for teammates, while a necromancer can add a fiery effect to the party’s weapons. These designs make the game look intent on challenging conventional MMORPG approaches to movement and cooperation, but its long-term content and community commitments cannot be confirmed by a single preview.

entry.title: A PS2 Fails During Play After More Than 20 Years, Turning Its Final Scene into Something Uncanny (translated)
entry.summary: A PlayStation 2 that had been used for more than 20 years suffered a serious hardware failure while running Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2, and the player recorded the console’s final moments of operation. The game’s track textures, vehicle geometry, and colours gradually warped. Instead of cutting directly to a black screen, it left behind a glitch scene resembling an abstract image. The article attributes the failure to ageing components, possibly solder joints beneath the graphics processor chip or video RAM. The Reddit community r/crtgaming viewed the retirement process as an old console’s farewell left behind during use.

entry.title: Persona 4 Revival Reveals a Character Trailer for Kanji Tatsumi (translated)
entry.summary: Persona 4 Revival has released a character trailer focused on Kanji Tatsumi. The source quotes the trailer’s introduction to the character, describing him as “a first-year high school student with an intimidating reputation as a delinquent,” giving players an early look at how the remake will present an established character from the original. At present, only this character video has been made public. There is no verifiable information yet about how the remake will rewrite the story, adjust its characters, or rearrange other content.

entry.title: Former Valve Developer Discusses the Development Challenges and Leaked Trailer of Left 4 Dead 2 (translated)
entry.summary: Veteran Valve writer Chet Faliszek looked back on the development of Left 4 Dead 2, discussing the recording process for the characters’ voices at the time as well as the leak of a game trailer. These memories bring the familiar finished product back to the production floor, showing how the characters took shape through voice recording and how the leaked promotional material became part of the team’s experience. The article offers a participant’s retrospective view of past work; it does not change the game content of Left 4 Dead 2 as it existed at the time.

entry.title: Savvy Signs Memoranda of Understanding with Gosu and Warpzone (translated)
entry.summary: During LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, Savvy Games Group signed two memoranda of understanding with Gosu Academy and Warpzone AI Labs. The agreement with Gosu Academy explores education in games and esports, including employment preparation, experiential and gamified learning, and simulated training. The agreement with Warpzone AI Labs focuses on knowledge transfer and mentorship for AI-native game development, and the parties will also assess establishing a local R&D lab dedicated to developing and testing AI-native games. Both memoranda emphasise building local skills and expertise. They remain exploratory, with no specific courses, jobs, or products confirmed yet.

entry.title: DMCC Releases a Post-Gamescom Report on Game Financing (translated)
entry.summary: During Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, the DMCC Gaming Centre held a closed-door roundtable and later released a report titled Financing the Future of Gaming. Participants included game-studio founders, publishers, investors, payment specialists, and technology providers. The report examines whether gaming’s financial infrastructure can keep pace as more studios self-publish, operate across borders, and control their own distribution and monetisation. It identifies several issues: investment channels focused on games, rising user-acquisition and distribution costs, local payment infrastructure, and regulatory challenges involved in expanding across borders. The report also argues that games should be treated as an independent investable category rather than using models borrowed from technology, media, or traditional project finance.

entry.title: Brian Ward Confirms His Departure from Savvy Games Group (translated)
entry.summary: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward confirmed his departure after fulfilling his contractual obligations to Savvy and its owner, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), bringing his five-year leadership tenure to an end. Bloomberg first reported the news on September 1, saying that PIF vice president and head of international investments Turqi Alnowaiser would become acting CEO. Ward wrote on LinkedIn that after more than 40 years of work, it was time to begin a new chapter and leave full-time employment, though he had been invited to remain as an adviser to the company. He moved to Riyadh in 2021 to establish Savvy, and during his tenure oversaw investments in and acquisitions of companies including Scopely, ESL, and FACEIT.

entry.title: AMD Adrenalin 26.9.1 Fixes Crashes in Apex Legends and Starfield (translated)
entry.summary: AMD has released the Adrenalin 26.9.1 driver. In addition to supporting Onimusha: Way of the Sword and The Blood of Dawnwalker, it also fixes potential crashes affecting the Radeon RX 9000 series in Apex Legends and Starfield. The update also addresses Smart Access Memory potentially being disabled after installing Windows 10, as well as an incorrect Anti-Lag 2 display status in Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy. However, RX 9050 4GB players are still advised to lower or disable graphics features that place a heavy load on the card when playing Cyberpunk 2077.

entry.title: Intel’s New Gaming Processors Reportedly Delayed Until 2027 (translated)
entry.summary: A leaked product roadmap indicates that mass production of Intel Nova Lake-S could begin in the fourth quarter of 2026, while the Core Ultra 400 series may not launch until the first quarter of 2027, differing from the originally expected late-2026 schedule. Intel has not announced an official launch date, so the reported delay remains unconfirmed. If the timeline is accurate, PC players waiting for the new platform will have to postpone their upgrades and may also face additional platform costs from LGA 1954 motherboards; meanwhile, AMD will have more time to prepare its next-generation Ryzen processors.

entry.title: NVIDIA Confirms DLSS 5 Will Support the RTX 40 Series (translated)
entry.summary: NVIDIA has confirmed that, after completing optimization for the RTX 50 series, DLSS 5 will also support the GeForce RTX 40 series. This technology is more than traditional upscaling: it uses 3D-guided neural rendering to improve lighting, materials, skin, hair, and other visual details. However, RTX 40 users will still need to wait for further information, and the actual results will depend on graphics-card performance, game support, and driver optimization.

entry.title: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Reveals Character Customization Introduction Video: New Android Race Joins the Battle, Players Can Learn from More Than 130 Characters (translated)
entry.summary: Bandai Namco has released a new video for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, placing customizable avatars at the center of its promotion and showcasing appearance options, combat setups, and character-development directions. The game is currently confirmed to offer six races and more than 130 characters whose abilities can be learned, with Androids added as a selectable race so players can build their own warriors according to their preferences. These features suggest that avatars are not merely a visual projection of the player, but are also connected to choices in combat style; however, the information available so far does not explain whether different setups will actually change how players act within the game world.

entry.title: Mobile Survival Horror Game The Phenomenon Arrives on Steam (translated)
entry.summary: This survival horror game, first released on mobile devices in 2015, is now getting a Steam version, giving a work originally constrained by mobile hardware and its era a renewed entry point into the modern PC gaming environment. For players, the port does more than add another purchasing platform: it also turns the preservation of an older title into a more concrete option. However, the available information does not yet explain whether the Steam version fully retains the original experience or what differences there are in controls and content, so further version details or hands-on experience will still be needed for confirmation.

entry.title: ZENONIA 1: The Line of Memories Launches on Steam (translated)
entry.summary: The origin of the ZENONIA series, first released on feature phones and accumulating 63 million downloads, arrived on Steam on August 31. This port has been optimized for modern environments, with adjustments to the interface and ease of control, so the old game no longer has to remain only a memory and can be played again through the more accessible PC platform. For returning veterans, the updates lower the barrier to revisiting the game; however, whether these convenience improvements also alter the original pacing still needs to be judged through actual play.

entry.title: The Forensic Mystery Adventure The Fleming Mansion Murder Case Is Scheduled for Release on November 3 (translated)
entry.summary: Set in England in 1959, this forensic mystery adventure game is scheduled for release on November 3. Players will begin by investigating the cause of death, gradually organizing clues and pursuing a serial murder case; the game's core is not moving quickly through scenes, but observing details and developing their own deductions. This design makes the investigation process itself part of the game, which may appeal more to players who enjoy slowly piecing together an answer; however, the available information does not yet explain whether the actual pacing will offer enough flexibility or how burdensome it will be to repeatedly recheck clues.

entry.title: Former Director of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Says Generative AI Is Widely Used in Game Development, Sparking Controversy (translated)
entry.summary: Daniel Vávra, former director of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2, said that game developers now widely use generative AI, suggesting that some people are simply afraid of being criticized and therefore unwilling to discuss it openly. His statement is currently a personal opinion, and the available description provides no industry survey sufficient to verify the claim of “widespread use,” so it cannot be treated directly as a picture of the industry as a whole. The real question left by the debate is whether development teams should disclose the extent of their AI use, and whether players can adequately judge how a work was made when that information is unavailable.

entry.title: Steam PvE Survival-Building Game Fest Kicks Off (translated)
entry.summary: Valve launched the Steam PvE Survival-Building Game Fest on September 1, allowing players to browse, from a single themed page, games built around survival and crafting as their core gameplay loop. The event’s value lies in bringing similar games scattered across the platform together, so players can first narrow down a shortlist based on theme and gameplay before deciding for themselves whether a title is worth playing or buying; the information provided so far does not specify the event’s duration, the number of included games, or the details of individual discounts.

entry.title: Xbox CEO Refuses to Confirm Whether Project Helix Has a Disc Drive (translated)
entry.summary: The Xbox CEO has not confirmed whether the next-generation console Project Helix will include a disc drive, so the hardware’s actual form remains undecided. The issue is not merely that one feature is missing from the specification sheet: for players who own physical games, the disc drive will affect whether their existing collections can continue to be used, as well as their options for resale and offline play. What is known at this stage is that key hardware decisions have not been made public; the available information confirms nothing about the final version, launch arrangements, or how existing games will be supported.

entry.title: World of Warcraft to scrub illegitimate Mythic+ dungeon rankings (translated)
entry.summary: Blizzard is preparing a comprehensive cleanup of illegitimate records in the World of Warcraft Mythic+ dungeon rankings, because paid boosting had pushed some legitimately playing players out of the top 1% reward bracket. The process will initially target rankings that already exist, with the aim of restoring the basic fairness players rely on when comparing their performance; however, Blizzard has also said that the ranking rules may continue to change. The information currently available does not specify the precise scope of the cleanup, when it will be carried out, or which records will be deemed illegitimate.

entry.title: Sandcastle Becomes a Popular New Steam Demo, Letting Players Dig in the Sand for Five Hours (translated)
entry.summary: Sandcastle’s beach-themed demo puts digging in the sand and building castles at its core, and a Polygon writer described spending five hours with it despite having no high-pressure objectives. Players can build castles at their own pace, or simply play in the sand along the coast, allowing the game to preserve merely staying and exploring as valid ways to play. The experience suggests that low-pressure interaction can sustain extended engagement, but the available information concerns only the demo and the writer’s experience; the full version’s content and release plans have not yet been confirmed.

entry.title: PlayStation State of Play and Japan Showcase to Air Back-to-Back on September 3 (translated)
entry.summary: PlayStation has announced that two programs will air back-to-back on the evening of September 3, allowing players to receive new-game information related to the platform and the Japanese market in one night. The announcement includes news about PlayStation Studios, third-party partners, and Square Enix titles, indicating that the company has scheduled updates from different sources within the same viewing period. This concentrated broadcast makes it convenient for players to catch up on developments at once, but it may also push attention toward a short-lived peak; the information currently provided does not specify the details of each title, the broadcast order, or whether release information will be announced.

entry.title: How Game Rumours Are Repackaged: A Look at the History of the GTA 6 Leak (translated)
entry.summary: The article looks back, in a parodic manner, at how information about GTA 6 began as anonymous rumours, passed through media reports, and eventually evolved into a major leak. It particularly points out that some details later proven true had already been circulating amid a large volume of unverified claims; this history is therefore not simply a story about guesses turning out to be correct, but also reflects how difficult it is for players to distinguish confirmed information from unverified rumours during heated discussions.

entry.title: Board Game Arena Adds a New Board Game Every Day for 31 Days (translated)
entry.summary: Board Game Arena's 2026 Summer Event ended on August 31. For 31 consecutive days during the event, one board game officially joined the platform each day. The article compiles the works added during this period, showing how a seasonal event can grow from a short-term project into a month-long stream of content; players gain more options to play, but must also deal with the rhythm of returning every day to check for something new.

entry.title: The Live-Action Street Fighter Actress Built Muscle to Recreate Chun-Li (translated)
entry.summary: To present Chun-Li's fighting style, which centers on leg techniques, in the live-action film, Karina Liang revealed in an interview with Empire that she trained in taekwondo, Muay Thai, and martial arts for two hours every day during filming, while also following a high-protein diet to build muscle. While gaining weight, she ate 12 eggs a day and had a meal every two hours; by the end of filming, each of her thighs had increased by about 6.5 centimeters. She also downloaded different versions of Street Fighter onto a PS5 and recorded Chun-Li's movements to study them in slow motion. The film is being produced by Legendary Entertainment and is scheduled for release on October 16, 2026.

entry.title: SD Gundam G Generation Eternal Launches New UR Unit Supply (translated)
entry.summary: Bandai Namco updated SD Gundam G Generation Eternal on the 31st, launching several featured supplies of UR units and pilots on the App Store, Google Play, and DMM GAMES. These include the temporarily available Full Armor Hyaku Shiki Kai (EX) and D Gundam Unit 3 (EX), with the event running until September 23 at 10:59 (GMT+8). The update also brings back Generation Tower EAST TOWER Floors 1–20, adds a 500-day login campaign offering up to 3,000 diamonds, and opens the Strong Enemy Incoming event featuring Nedicks; the three activities run until October 5, October 1, and September 17 at 10:59 (GMT+8), respectively.

entry.title: 007 First Light Switch 2 Version Delayed for the Third Time (translated)
entry.summary: This is already the third delay for the Switch 2 version, creating a clear gap between the earlier claim that development was progressing smoothly and the latest news. The new release date remains undetermined in the information currently available, so players still cannot plan when to buy or play it.

entry.title: Pokémon: Wild Card Movie Announced for 2027 (translated)
entry.summary: The planned 2027 release first places this film on players’ list of future possibilities. IGN reports that the Pokémon: Wild Card movie has been announced, but the information currently available provides no further plot or release details.

entry.title: Phantom Blade Zero Tops Steam’s Best-Sellers Chart as Demand Builds Ahead of Its State of Play Showcase (translated)
entry.summary: Demand from the Chinese market has pushed Phantom Blade Zero to the top of Steam’s global best-sellers chart. The ranking appeared ahead of the dedicated State of Play livestream, showing that player interest has already turned into pre-orders or purchases.

entry.title: Steam Weekly Roundup Reveals the Ten Most Popular Game Genres (translated)
entry.summary: A weekly ranking distills Steam’s popular genres as of August 30 into ten options, helping players quickly scan the market. Popularity can show where collective attention is focused, but it cannot directly determine which genre suits a particular player.

entry.title: Elden Ring’s Highroad Fort Suddenly Fills with Messages Making Players See “Things That Don’t Exist” (translated)
entry.summary: A familiar fortress is suddenly covered with mysterious messages, causing players to notice sights that were never there. The phenomenon emerges from a combination of community interaction and environmental interpretation; the game world has not officially gained new content.

entry.title: EGDF Publishes 2024 European Games Industry Insights Data (translated)
entry.summary: The 6,600 studios and more than 95,000 workers form the substantial foundation keeping Europe’s games industry running. EGDF says the report compiles 2024 industry data from 28 European countries and highlights the sector’s resilience.

entry.title: EU designates ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under the Digital Services Act (translated)
entry.summary: Under the Digital Services Act, the European Commission has designated Roblox and Reddit as very large online platforms and listed ChatGPT as a very large online search engine. All three services reported an average of 45 million monthly users in the EU, meaning they must meet additional obligations by January 2027, including assessing and reducing systemic risks related to illegal content, impacts on minors, mental and physical health, fundamental rights, electoral processes and public security.
